name: integrated_autonomy_world
description: og-08's off-gradient test inside ONE persistent world assembled from the merged phases: the lineage lives on what real processes deliver — the external pmf tapped through its membrane leak and an internal store charged by the drive its live substrate pool sustains (an energy_coupling class, the STORAGE MODEL), organic carbon reaching it through a localization class (the TRANSPORT LAW) and the Phase-8 exchange rules at a boundary class's leakiness (the PERMEABILITY ASSUMPTION), the Phase-3 universe inside it catalysed by the mineral surface or by the machinery its heredity class holds (the INHERITANCE CLASS), upkeep priced by a MAINTENANCE LAW, and a population of individuals that divide and go extinct by structural rewrites. An AblationStep withdraws the gradient, the mineral access and the feed; pump (coupling_activity), importer (the ActiveUptakeRule) and heredity (attachment) are the three innovations; environment=generic is the og-adv reject control. Seven ledgers run beside the world and a structural-event log records every event. The vent endmembers are one Phase-1 posterior draw (vg-data integrated_autonomy).

ablation.doc:
Schedule the withdrawal of the three geological drivers.

Each driver's support fraction holds at 1 until ``start`` (world seconds),
relaxes linearly to its ocean floor over ``duration`` and stays there — the
off-gradient test of og-08 as a scheduled perturbation of ONE persistent
world rather than a parameter sweep. ``environment = "generic"`` is the
og-adv reject control: every driver sits at its floor from t = 0 (no
sustained H2 feed, no mineral catalyst, no gradient). Publishes the three
fractions, the ablation phase (0 hold, 1 withdrawing, 2 withdrawn) and the
structural events it causes.

_contract.summary: Scheduled withdrawal of the geological drivers (gradient, mineral access, feed) toward their ocean floors — the off-gradient test as a perturbation of one persistent world.
_contract.description: support_X(t) = 1 for t < start; 1 - (1 - floor_X) (t - start) / duration while withdrawing; floor_X after. environment = 'generic' holds every driver at its floor from t = 0 (the og-adv reject control). Publishes the fractions, the phase and the ablation events.

outputs.feed_support: fraction of vent fluid delivered to the pore (0-1)

assumptions: Linear, simultaneous withdrawal of the three drivers (a controlled perturbation, not a cell upgrade).

drivers.doc:
Turn the support fractions into the physical drivers the phases read.

The vent endmembers are one Phase-1 posterior draw (dissolved H2, ΔpH, T);
the ocean endmembers are the Hadean-ocean floors. Publishes the external
pmf (``electric_potential``), the vent-side pH the interface sees, the
FeS catalyst activity, the dissolved H2 at the interface and the LIVE pore
feed (universe species → molar): H2 and the inorganic N / P scaled by the
feed fraction, CO2 from the ocean (never withdrawn), and the organic feed
scaled by the feed fraction AND by the interface's net carbon flux relative
to its in-vent steady state (the running maximum during the hold) — so the
feed collapses when any driver the fixation chemistry needs is withdrawn.

_contract.summary: Posterior vent endmembers x support fractions -> pmf, interface pH, catalyst activity, interface H2 and the live pore feed (organics scaled by the fixation class's relative carbon flux).
_contract.description: electric_potential = pmf(dpH, T) gradient_support; pH_vent = pH_ocean + dpH gradient_support; catalyst_activity = max(mineral_access, 1e-6); H2_interface = H2_ocean + (H2_vent - H2_ocean) feed_support; pore feed: H2 as at the interface, CO2 = DIC, pyruvate = feed_pyruvate feed_support (J_C / J_C,ref), ammonium / phosphate scaled by feed_support.

serpentinization.doc:
Reduced serpentinization source: ``(T, flow) -> H2 / alkalinity / heat``.

REDUCED REPRODUCTION, not PHREEQC/Reaktoro. Each tick it (a) adds the
integrated H2 + alkalinity + heat it produced over the interval to the vent
stores (bare ``float`` deltas, so they accumulate and compose), and (b)
publishes the instantaneous source *rates* as ``overwrite[float]`` sensor
readings for observability. Production peaks in a temperature window and
scales with water flux (serpentinization is water–rock-reaction limited).

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

conservation_ledger.doc: Integrate published source rates and audit them against the accumulated pools.

_contract.summary: Conservation ledger: integrates source rates and audits pools, charge, flux and energy directionality.
_contract.description: Every tick, integrates the H2 / alkalinity / heat source rates the serpentinization class publishes and compares the running integral with the pools the composite accumulated (the matter + energy ledger — exact by construction when every process writes additive deltas to the same store). Tracks the worst-case PHREEQC charge imbalance and the FVM flux divergence residual, and a directionality witness (serpentinization heat is released, never absorbed). ledger_ok = 1 when every residual is below the configured tolerance.

outputs.H2_in: integrated H2 source (same units as the pool)
outputs.energy_directionality: 1 if the heat source has never been negative, else 0
outputs.ledger_ok: 1 if every residual is within tolerance, else 0

assumptions: Every process writing the audited pools returns additive deltas (bare float), so the pool equals the running integral of the published rates.
The ledger runs at the same interval as the source process, so it reads each published rate exactly once.

fixation.doc:
Carbon fixation as a galvanic cell across the Fe/Ni-sulfide wall: Nernst
half-cell potentials from the fluid redox state, Butler-Volmer electrode
kinetics with Koutecky-Levich transport limits, the ohmic mineral + ionic
circuit, and the faradaic split of the current over formate / acetate /
pyruvate (additive deltas on the dissolved pool) with open-flow washout.
Publishes the circuit readouts, the four failure-mode loss fractions and the
electron-balance witnesses the charge ledger audits.

_contract.summary: Butler-Volmer galvanic cell: fluid redox -> Nernst potentials -> overpotentials -> current -> surface rates.
_contract.description: Each tick solves the vent-wall cell at steady state: H2 oxidation on the alkaline side and CO2 reduction (plus competing H2 evolution) on the acidic side, with Butler-Volmer kinetics scaled by catalyst activity, Ni fraction and temperature, Koutecky-Levich transport limits, and the ohmic drop through the mineral layer (thickness / conductivity) and the pore-fluid return path. The CO2-reduction current is split over formate (2e), acetate (8e) and pyruvate (10e) by electron branch fractions calibrated to the Preiner-2020 yield hierarchy; product increments are additive deltas with exponential open-flow washout. Publishes emf, overpotential, current density, faradaic efficiency, the anode / cathode-branch electron fluxes, the circuit residual and the thermodynamic / electrical / catalytic / transport loss fractions with the dominant limitation code.

inputs.H2: dissolved H2 on the vent side (molar)
inputs.CO2: dissolved CO2 on the ocean side (molar)
inputs.ni_fraction: Ni mole fraction of the Fe/Ni catalytic phase
inputs.conductivity: electronic conductivity of the mineral layer (S/m)

outputs.emf: open-circuit emf at the current product level (volt)
outputs.overpotential: total overpotential + ohmic drop under load (volt)
outputs.faradaic_efficiency: fraction of the electrons reaching the cathode that reduce CO2
outputs.electron_flux: electrons supplied to the cathode: cell current + local ocean-side H2 oxidation (mole/second)
outputs.iv_residual: circuit-equation residual at the solved current (dimensionless)
outputs.loss_thermodynamic: fraction of the fresh-fluid emf lost to product back-pressure
outputs.loss_electrical: fraction lost to the ohmic drop

math: E_a = -(RT/F) ln10 pH_vent - (RT/2F) ln a_H2;  E_c = E0 - (RT/F) ln10 pH_ocean + (RT/2F) ln(a_CO2 / a_HCOOH)
j = j0 [exp(alpha F eta / RT) - exp(-(1-alpha) F eta / RT)];  1/j_eff = 1/j_kin + 1/j_lim
E_c(j) - E_a(j) = j (L/sigma_e + L/(sigma_f phi^1.5))
rate_i = f_i FE j A / (n_i F)
assumptions: Steady cell each tick (electrode double layers equilibrate faster than the pools change).
The CO2/HCOOH couple sets the cathode emf; acetate and pyruvate are side branches of the same current (their couples are more positive, so this is conservative).
H2 and CO2 are boundary feeds (not depleted by the current); products accumulate and wash out.
Standard potentials taken at 25 C (dE0/dT neglected); Henry constants van 't Hoff-corrected.

charge_ledger.doc:
Charge + electron-count ledger for the electrochemical interface (Phase 2).

Sits beside a ``carbon_fixation`` class and audits, every tick, the three
electron rates it publishes: the anode-side rate (``electron_flux``, the
current through the mineral) against the two cathode branches
(``carbon_electron_flux`` into formate / acetate / pyruvate and
``her_electron_flux`` into hydrogen evolution). Kirchhoff's node law makes
``charge_residual = |anode - (carbon + her)| / anode`` zero for a correctly
wired class; the faradaic efficiency is recomputed as ``carbon / anode`` and
must never exceed 1; the circuit's current-voltage residual (published by
the Butler-Volmer class at its solved operating point) is tracked worst-case.
Integrates the charge passed (coulomb) and the electrons delivered to carbon
(mole) for the report, and publishes ``charge_ledger_ok``.

_contract.summary: Charge + electron ledger: Kirchhoff residual per tick, faradaic efficiency <= 1, current-voltage residual.
_contract.description: Every tick compares the anode-side electron rate a carbon-fixation class publishes with the sum of its cathode branches (carbon products + hydrogen evolution): charge_residual = |anode - (carbon + her)| / anode. Recomputes the faradaic efficiency as carbon / anode and tracks that it never exceeds 1, tracks the worst-case circuit (current-voltage) residual, integrates the charge passed and the electrons delivered to carbon, and publishes charge_ledger_ok = 1 while every residual is inside tolerance.

inputs.iv_residual: circuit residual at the solved current (dimensionless)

outputs.faradaic_efficiency: carbon / anode this tick (0 when no current)
outputs.faradaic_efficiency_max: worst-case faradaic efficiency so far (must be <= 1)
outputs.charge_ledger_ok: 1 while every residual is within tolerance and FE <= 1

math: charge_residual = |e_anode - (e_carbon + e_her)| / e_anode
FE = e_carbon / e_anode <= 1
assumptions: The class publishes the three electron rates from the same solved operating point.

localization.doc:
Reduced multisolute pore-network surrogate (uv ``.venv``, no dolfinx).

Per species, the steady dissolved-pool enrichment is
``exp(beta) * mobile_fraction * degradation_factor`` where
``beta = geom * (S_T * dT) * washout(Pe) * (1 - porosity)`` (the single-tracer
reduced model, per species, calibrated to the FEM reference),
``washout(Pe) = 1/(1 + Pe/pe0)`` (a FLOW-THROUGH pore de-concentrates as
advection dominates -- enrichment is strongest at low Peclet), ``Pe`` is the
species' advective Peclet = ``peclet * D_mean/D`` (the control ``peclet`` is
set at the mixture-mean diffusivity), ``mobile_fraction = k_des/(k_ads+k_des)``
(adsorption removes a species from the dissolved pool), and
``degradation_factor = 1/(1 + k_deg * residence)``. Honours the
``spatial_transport`` face.

network_cell-0.doc:
The Phase-3 reaction universe inside ONE protocell, masked to a lineage
repertoire, integrated by its own libRoadRunner instance each tick.

_contract.summary: A protocell's real reaction network: the Phase-3 rule-generated C/H/O universe (libRoadRunner) masked to the lineage's catalyst repertoire, closed inside the membrane; publishes what it produced itself.
_contract.description: Reads the agent's dissolved pool from the agents map, loads it into the agent's own libRoadRunner model of the Phase-3 universe (413 reversible reactions, eQuilibrator dG', catalyst-site saturation, degradation to tar) with the lineage's rule mask applied as 0/1 rate multipliers, advances the chemistry over the tick with no exchange term (exchange is the SpatialCouplingStep's reactive system), and writes the concentration deltas back. Publishes the product classes the agent PRODUCED this tick (net internal production above the flux floor — not presence, which may come from uptake), the per-rule flux, the H2 consumption and CO2 fixation rates, the Phase-3 witnesses (exact element residual, dissipation, carbon degraded) and the agent's organic carbon.

inputs.internal: the agent's dissolved pool (molar, keyed by universe species id)

outputs.internal: concentration deltas after the tick's chemistry (molar)
outputs.functions_produced: product classes with gross internal production above flux_floor this tick (1/0)
outputs.rule_flux: sum of |v_r| over the reactions of each rule (molar/second)
outputs.net_carbon_flux: net CO2 fixed into organics (mole/second, per agent)
outputs.h2_consumption: net H2 consumed by internal reactions (mole/second)
outputs.co2_fixation: net CO2 consumed by internal reactions (mole/second)
outputs.dissipation: -sum_r v_r dG_r (watt, per agent; >= 0 for consistent kinetics)
outputs.element_residual: max |E S| over the agent's reactions (exact; 0 for the universe)
outputs.total_organic_carbon: organic carbon inside the agent (molar C)

assumptions: Operator splitting per tick: chemistry inside the agent, then exchange through the membrane (the reactive system).
A lineage is a set of reaction rules its catalysts carry; uncatalysed decarboxylations belong to every lineage.
The agent's volume is fixed this phase (no growth / division); positions are fixed (no motion).

coupling.doc: Couple the agents onto the pore field and fire the exchange rules.

_contract.summary: Points each agent at a pore-field cell (fixed positions), shapes the cells' background from the Phase-4 enrichment, and fires the matter-exchange rules (uptake, secretion, diffusion, feed/washout) with firing counts.
_contract.description: Every tick after the agents' chemistry: builds the reactive-system context from the agents map (interior pools, volumes, per-species membrane rate constants P A / V from the permeability classes), the field cells and each cell's background — the feed scaled by the localization class's per-species enrichment raised to the cell's fractional position along the pore (the Soret profile) — and applies the BigraphicalReactiveSystem's rules. Writes the exchange deltas back to the agents' pools and the cells, and publishes per-rule firing counts and moles, the cross-lineage flux of every species (moles secreted by one lineage and taken up by another this tick), the per-element inflow / outflow across the pore boundary (for the element ledger) and each agent's uptake / secretion.

inputs.lineages: per-agent lineage id and position along the pore
inputs.field: pore field cells (map of dissolved pools)
inputs.enrichment: Phase-4 per-species enrichment at the trap end (dimensionless)

outputs.cross_lineage_flux: per species, moles moved between lineages this tick
outputs.inflow: cumulative moles of C / N / P fed into the pore
outputs.exchange: per-agent uptake / secretion this tick (moles) and lineage

assumptions: Agents do not move (Phase-8 decision: point agents on the fields first; motion deferred).
Exchange is linear permeation; the tick's transfer is the exact two-compartment relaxation.

active_import.doc:
Fire the :class:`~viva_genesis.ecology.reactive_system.ActiveUptakeRule`
for every agent: a saturable transporter (``v_max`` per substrate at full
machinery, scaled by the lineage's machinery) moving the configured
substrates from the agent's field cell into the agent against their
gradient, regulated like a transporter: it runs only while the inside is
below its set-point (``targets``, a fraction of the in-vent level) and
spends at most ``budget_fraction`` of the lineage's work supply per tick.
Conserving (the same moles leave the cell and enter the agent); counted;
its thermodynamic cost (RT ln(c_in / c_out) per mole uphill, over the
transporter efficiency) is published as ``import_power`` for the work
budget. ``importer = "off"`` is the knockout (no rule fires). A Process (not
a Step): it exchanges with the same agents and field the coupling step
does, and steps must form a DAG — the rule fires once per world tick.

_contract.summary: The importer innovation as a counted, conserving exchange rule: saturable active uptake against the gradient, costing RT ln(c_in/c_out) per mole from the work budget.
_contract.description: Builds the reactive-system context from the agents map and the field, gives every agent an importer capacity v_max x machinery per substrate, fires ActiveUptakeRule and writes the deltas back; publishes the moles imported per species this tick, the organic carbon imported per second, the import power and the cumulative firings.
assumptions: Michaelis-Menten transporter regulated to an inside / outside ratio cap; thermodynamic minimum cost of concentration over a fixed coupling efficiency.

element_ledger.doc:
Element ledger ACROSS agents and fields (Phase 8).

Sits beside the ``proto_ecology`` agents and the ``SpatialCouplingStep``
and, every tick, sums the carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus held by **every
agent's interior and every field cell** (``moles = concentration x
volume``, element counts from the universe's exact formulas plus the
inorganic N / P solutes) and compares the total with the only sources and
sinks of the metacommunity: the pore's feed inflow and washout outflow
(integrated per element by the coupling step's pore-exchange rule) and the
carbon the agents' networks degraded to tar (each agent's roadrunner
integrator). Membrane uptake / secretion and pore diffusion move matter
between places of the bigraph and must leave the total untouched — the
same float leaves one place and enters the other — so

    total_X(t) = total_X(0) + in_X - out_X - degraded_X        (X = C, N, P)

holds at integrator tolerance for carbon (the network's CVODE run) and at
round-off for N and P (no chemistry transforms them in the C/H/O
universe — the ledger is in place for the N/P-bearing rule set). Also
integrates the exchange-rule firing counts and publishes one
``element_ledger_ok``.

_contract.summary: Cross-system element ledger: C / N / P summed over every agent and field cell must equal the initial total plus pore inflow minus washout minus tar, every tick; exchange-rule firings integrated.
_contract.description: Sums C, N and P over the agents' interiors and the field cells (concentration x volume x element count), reads the coupling step's cumulative per-element pore inflow / outflow and the agents' cumulative carbon degraded to tar, and publishes the relative residual of the balance per element, the worst case so far, the cumulative exchange-rule firings and element_ledger_ok = 1 while every residual is within tolerance. Membrane exchange and pore diffusion are internal transfers and must not appear in the balance.

inputs.inflow: cumulative moles of C / N / P fed by the pore
inputs.rates: per-agent cumulative carbon degraded to tar (mole)

outputs.C_residual: |C_total - C0 - (in - out - degraded)| / max(C0 + in, eps)
outputs.carbon_degraded: cumulative carbon to tar over all agents (mole)
outputs.exchange_firings_total: cumulative firings of every exchange rule
outputs.element_ledger_ok: 1 while every residual is within tolerance

math: total_X(t) = total_X(0) + in_X - out_X - degraded_X
assumptions: The coupling step integrates the pore boundary flows exactly (analytic relaxation); the agents' tar integrators carry CVODE tolerance, so the carbon tolerance is the integrator's, not round-off.

network_ledger.doc:
Element + free-energy ledger over an open chemical network (Phase 3).

Sits beside a ``proto_metabolism`` class and audits, every tick, the three
witnesses the class publishes:

* ``element_residual`` — ``max |E S|`` over the network's internal
  reactions (exact algebra, independent of the integrator): a generated
  universe is balanced by construction; a lumped reaction such as og-02's
  ``OAA + 2 CO2 -> 2 OAA + acetate`` or a rewired null is not, and the
  ledger says so.
* ``carbon_residual`` — the integrated carbon balance
  ``|TOC - TOC0 - (fed + fixed - washed - degraded)| / TOC``, which must stay
  at the integrator's tolerance.
* ``dissipation`` — ``-Σ v_r ΔG_r`` over internal reactions; the second
  law requires it to be non-negative every tick (free-energy
  directionality). ``free_energy_in >= work + dissipated`` of the roadmap
  reduces, for a reactor with no work output, to this inequality.

Publishes the worst-case residuals so far, the directionality witness and
one ``ledger_ok`` flag, mirroring :class:`ConservationLedgerProcess`.

_contract.summary: Element + free-energy ledger over an open reaction network: stoichiometric element residual, integrated carbon balance, dissipation >= 0.
_contract.description: Audits the witnesses a proto_metabolism class publishes each tick: the exact stoichiometric element residual max|E S| (0 for a rule-generated universe; non-zero exposes lumped or rewired reactions that create or destroy atoms), the integrated carbon-balance residual (must sit at integrator tolerance) and the free-energy dissipation -sum v dG (second law: never negative). ledger_ok = 1 while every witness is within tolerance.

outputs.free_energy_directionality: 1 if dissipation has never been below -tolerance
outputs.ledger_ok: 1 if every witness is within tolerance

assumptions: The network class computes the witnesses from its own stoichiometry and live rates; the ledger only accumulates and grades them.

boundary_class.doc:
Coarse-grained physico-chemical model of mixed single-chain amphiphile
vesicle self-assembly + permeability, calibrated to Jordan 2019. Reads the
environment (pH, ionic strength, temperature); decides vesicle viability from
the pH window + salt/divalent tolerance (broadened by the co-surfactant
fraction); and emits the membrane area, permeability, compartment volume,
viable-compartment count, and the retention / access / individuality-access
tradeoff. A reproduction, not a wrapped MD engine — labeled as such.

_contract.summary: Coarse-grained mixed-amphiphile vesicle self-assembly + permeability, calibrated to Jordan 2019: the individuality-vs-access tradeoff (retain chemistry while staying permeable to the gradient).
_contract.description: Clean-room reproduction of the Jordan-2019 vesicle-stability physical chemistry (NOT a wrapped MD engine; the proposed primary method is coarse-grained membrane kinetics). Vesicles are viable when pH lies in a band around the bilayer apparent pKa AND ionic strength / divalent cations stay below a tolerance that the co-surfactant fraction broadens; permeability follows a solubility-diffusion Arrhenius law; retention = exp(-P*A/V*tau) and access = P*A*gradient trade off, their product non-empty only in an intermediate window. Favorable (mixed amphiphiles, alkaline, seawater salt) forms viable compartments with retention AND access; a single-fatty-acid control fails on salt tolerance.

outputs.individuality_access: retention x access — individuality without isolation (dimensionless)

math: viable = (|pH - pKa_eff| < window_eff) and (I < I_max_eff) and (Mg < Mg_max_eff) and (T in range)
P = P0 * exp(-Ea/(R*T)) * (1 + k_P * mix_fraction)
retention = exp(-P*A/V*tau);  access = tanh(P*A*gradient_scale);  individuality_access = retention*access

symbols.pKa_eff: bilayer apparent pKa (shifted up from solution)

assumptions: Coarse-grained reproduction calibrated to Jordan 2019; full membrane MD is out of environment.
Vesicle viability: pH in [pKa_eff +/- window] AND ionic_strength < I_max AND divalent < Mg_max AND T in range.
Co-surfactant fraction broadens the pH / salt / divalent tolerance (the Jordan mixed-amphiphile result).
Permeability: solubility-diffusion Arrhenius in T + composition; retention/access from P*A/V.

energy.doc:
``thioester_acyl_phosphate``: og-energy's thioester / acyl-phosphate
carrier as the internal store (bond 35 kJ/mol), leaking by hydrolysis and
slow carrier permeation — the existing currency, now inside the individual.

_contract.summary: Thioester / acyl-phosphate coupling: the og-energy chemical carrier as the individual's internal store.
_contract.description: The chemical drive charges a thioester-class carrier pool (bond 35 kJ/mol; potential bond + RT ln(q/(1-q))) while the drive clears the store potential; work is drawn once the potential clears the load; the store leaks by hydrolysis and by carrier permeation (ratio x P_H).

inputs.electric_potential: external ion gradient (natural pmf) across the membrane (volt)
inputs.drive_free_energy: chemical drive free energy per turnover (kJ/mol)
inputs.catalyst_activity: catalyst availability scaling both the external capture and the drive turnover (0-1)
inputs.drive_availability: optional (Phase 9): fraction of the drive turnover the live substrate pool sustains (0-1; 1 when unwired)

outputs.free_energy_in: gross free energy drawn from the environment this tick (watt)
outputs.external_power: useful work from the passive external tap (watt)
outputs.internal_power: useful work drawn from the internal store (watt)
outputs.dissipated: free energy dissipated this tick: uncaptured leak + charging drop + draw excess + store leak (watt)
outputs.leak_power: membrane-leak losses: uncaptured ion flux + store leak (watt)
outputs.net_power: work - maintenance (watt); the surplus the individual keeps
outputs.energy_stored: free energy held in the internal store (joule)

math: G_flux = F P_H A dc pmf;  external = eta_ext G_flux
charge: dq = a D (1-slip)(1-q) g(dG_drive - mu(q)) dt / N, capped at mu(q1) = dG_drive
draw: dq_d = k_draw q g(mu(q) - dG_load) dt;  work = min(G(q1)-G(q2), N dq_d dG_load)
leak: dq_l = lambda(P_H) q dt;  in = work + dissipated + dE (exact)
autonomy = internal / (internal + external)
assumptions: Per-individual SI power budget; coarse-grained deterministic kinetics (reproducible), not a wrapped engine.
The external tap needs membrane leak (G_flux = F P_H A dc pmf); the chemical drive needs none.
Work is delivered only when the store potential mu(q) clears the load free energy (soft gate ~RT).

free_energy_ledger.doc:
Free-energy ledger of an individual's power budget (Phase 6).

Sits beside an ``energy_coupling`` class and audits, every tick, the four
witnesses it publishes — ``free_energy_in`` (W, gross free energy drawn
from the environment), ``work`` (W, useful work delivered), ``dissipated``
(W) and ``energy_stored`` (J, the internal store) — against the roadmap's
invariant

    free_energy_in  >=  work + dissipated

taken cumulatively WITH the store: integrating the rates, ``in_cum + E(0)
- work_cum - diss_cum = E(t)`` must hold exactly (``free_energy_residual``
at rounding) and ``E(t) >= 0`` makes the inequality (``second_law_margin``
= ``in_cum + E0 - work_cum - diss_cum`` never negative). Per tick the
dissipation rate must never be negative (the directionality witness, as
:class:`NetworkLedgerProcess`) and the capture efficiency ``work_cum /
in_cum`` must never exceed 1. Publishes the worst cases so far and one
``free_energy_ledger_ok`` flag.

_contract.summary: Free-energy ledger of a protocell's power budget: free_energy_in >= work + dissipated (with the store), exact residual, dissipation >= 0, efficiency <= 1.
_contract.description: Integrates the gross free-energy intake, the useful work and the dissipation an energy_coupling class publishes and compares them with the store it reports: in_cum + E0 - work_cum - diss_cum must equal E(t) to rounding (free_energy_residual) and never go negative (second_law_margin); the per-tick dissipation rate must be >= -tolerance and work_cum / in_cum <= 1. free_energy_ledger_ok = 1 while every witness holds.

inputs.free_energy_in: gross free energy drawn from the environment (watt)
inputs.energy_stored: free energy held in the internal store (joule)

outputs.free_energy_residual: |in_cum + E0 - work_cum - diss_cum - E(t)| / max(in_cum, eps) this tick
outputs.second_law_margin: in_cum + E0 - work_cum - diss_cum (joule; must stay >= 0)
outputs.dissipation_min: minimum per-tick dissipation rate seen (negative = violation)
outputs.free_energy_ledger_ok: 1 while every witness is within tolerance

math: in_cum + E0 - work_cum - diss_cum = E(t)
free_energy_in >= work + dissipated  <=>  E(t) >= 0
assumptions: The class publishes the four witnesses from the same tick; the ledger only integrates and grades.

maintenance_demand.doc:
Price the lineage's upkeep under one of three maintenance laws (W per
individual), calibrated to coincide at the reference point (full machinery,
fatty-acid leakiness, pump on) and to differ in what they scale with:

* ``constant`` — ``m_base + m_active a`` (the Phase-6 law: upkeep follows
  the coupling activity INVESTED, ``a = coupling_activity`` while the pump
  is on, whatever machinery the lineage actually holds);
* ``leak_repair`` — ``m_base + m_active a x relative_leak`` (Sojo 2014: a
  leakier membrane costs proportionally more to keep energised);
* ``turnover`` — ``m_base + m_active x machinery`` (Lane & Martin 2012:
  re-synthesis of the machinery actually held, whether or not it is used).

_contract.summary: Maintenance power under one of three laws: constant (Phase 6), leak_repair (scales with membrane leakiness), turnover (scales with machinery held).
_contract.description: m = m_base + m_active a | m_base + m_active a rel_leak | m_base + m_active machinery (a = coupling_activity while the pump is on).

heredity_class.doc:
One heredity class on the face: shared pools in (molar) + energy store (J) +
the attachment flag -> lineage sensors, information + cost readouts, and the
consumption written back as additive deltas on the pools / store.

_contract.summary: Heredity class 'rna_like' on the heredity face: an L-site template copied template-directed with per-site fidelity q (Eigen ratchet with back-mutation), L nucleotides + L quanta per copy
_contract.description: The 'rna_like' heredity class, simulated as an exact Gillespie lineage at low copy number: an L-site template copied template-directed with per-site fidelity q (Eigen ratchet with back-mutation), L nucleotides + L quanta per copy. Draws integer precursor molecules from the shared dissolved pools and integer energy quanta from the shared stored-work store (matched budgets across classes), publishes the lineage sensors, the running parent-offspring mutual information with its convergence flag and the per-tick costs the information ledger integrates. Before attachment (attached = 0) daughters re-form their heritable state de novo at fission: og-06's non-heritable control.

outputs.information_content: realised heritable bits (parent-offspring MI net of the permutation null)
outputs.mi_converged: 1 when the MI ladder + bootstrap SE converged
outputs.replication_energy: energy quanta spent by heredity this tick, in joules
outputs.fidelity: mean parent->daughter heritable-state overlap at fission

assumptions: Exact SSA (direct method) within each tick; pools and store refreshed at tick boundaries.
Selection acts through growth: bulk grows at k_grow (1 + sigma phi); dilution is uniform at capacity.

lineage_supply.doc:
Feed the heredity class's shared pools and energy store from the
integrated world instead of a chemostat: each precursor pool relaxes
toward ``precursor_yield x total_organic_carbon`` (the fraction of the
cell's own organic carbon that is activated precursor; hypothetical) and
the store receives ``allocation x work x n_individuals`` per tick, capped —
published as ``work_flux`` so the information ledger stays exact.

_contract.summary: Precursor pools from the cell's own organic carbon and an energy allocation from its work — the heredity budgets of the integrated world.
_contract.description: pool += feed_rate (yield TOC - pool); stored_work += min(allocation work N dt, room); work_flux = that inflow.

information_ledger.doc:
Information ledger — heritable bits per unit energy (Phase 7).

Sits beside a ``heredity`` class and, every tick, (i) integrates the energy
the class spent on heredity (``replication_energy``: quanta × ΔG_quantum,
plus ``precursor_energy``: the precursors' free-energy equivalents) and
the offspring it produced, (ii) audits the shared energy store exactly —
``stored_work == W0 + ∫ work_flux − ∫ replication_energy`` (every process
writes additive deltas to the same store, so the residual is at float
round-off) — and (iii) prices the realised heritable information the
class publishes (``information_content``: parent→offspring mutual
information net of its permutation null, in bits) per joule and per
precursor molecule spent per offspring. The MI estimator's convergence flag
(``mi_converged``, the prefix-ladder + bootstrap check of
``viva_genesis.heredity.information``) gates ``information_ledger_ok``:
an unconverged estimate is reported but never certified.

_contract.summary: Information ledger: heritable bits per joule and per precursor, exact energy-store audit, MI convergence gate.
_contract.description: Integrates the energy a heredity class spends (quanta x dG_quantum + precursor free-energy equivalents) and the offspring it produces, audits the shared energy store against W0 + integrated inflow - integrated spend (exact when every process writes additive deltas), and prices the class's realised heritable bits (parent-offspring MI net of the permutation null) per joule and per precursor molecule per offspring. information_ledger_ok = 1 only while the energy residual is within tolerance AND the MI estimator has converged.

inputs.information_content: realised heritable bits (MI net of null) the class publishes
inputs.mi_converged: 1 when the MI prefix ladder + bootstrap SE converged
inputs.replication_energy: energy quanta spent on heredity this tick (joule)
inputs.precursor_energy: free-energy equivalent of precursors consumed this tick (joule)
inputs.work_flux: energy added to the store this tick (joule)

outputs.heritable_bits: the certified heritable bits (information_content when converged, else 0)

math: bits_per_joule = I(parent; offspring) / (E_heredity / births)
energy_residual = |W - (W0 + sum flux - sum used)| / sum flux
assumptions: Only the heredity class draws on the audited store; the feed is the only inflow.
The ledger runs at the same interval as the class and the feed, reading each published value once.

lineage_state.doc:
Read the lineage's heredity class and the cell's live pools into the
quantities the innovations run on.

* ``machinery`` = the heredity class's ``mean_function`` over its
  ``function_reference`` (the function level at which the lineage holds
  its full machinery; hypothetical), clipped to 1 — the catalytic capacity
  behind the pump and the importer. With heredity forced off the class
  still runs (daughters re-form their heritable state de novo), so the
  knockout's machinery is whatever the de novo state holds.
* ``catalysis_total`` = 1 - (1 - mineral_access)(1 - machinery): the
  mineral surface while on it, the lineage's own machinery once off it
  (drives the agent's mineral-catalysed rules).
* ``drive_availability`` = max(H2_in / (H2_in + K_H2), org_in / (org_in +
  K_org)) x machinery: the fraction of the drive turnover the cell's own
  substrate pool sustains, coupled by its machinery — the pump's live input.
* ``autonomy_information`` = machinery (1 - mineral_access) / catalysis_total:
  the share of the lineage's catalysis its heredity supplies.

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

autonomy_budget.doc:
Read what the phases deliver and publish the co-limited budget and the
continuous autonomy value, decomposed by function.

Work (W per individual): supply = external tap + internal store work
(the energy_coupling class); demand = maintenance (the maintenance law) +
import power (the active-uptake rule) + the heredity allocation. Material
(mol C/s): supply = passive organic uptake (the exchange rules, net of
secretion, clipped at 0) + active organic import + the cell's own CO2
fixation; demand = the carbon its network degrades to tar. Autonomy:
work = internal / (internal + external); material = (active + own fixation)
/ supply; total = work-weighted over both with carbon at its free-energy
equivalent. ``lineage_fitness`` = min(net work / P_scale, net material /
M_scale) (dimensionless, og-08's readout name).

_contract.summary: The integrated co-limited budget (work AND material) and the continuous autonomy value decomposed by function (work / material / information).
_contract.description: net_power = external + internal - maintenance - import - allocation x (external + internal); material_net = uptake_C + active_C + fixation_C - degraded_C; autonomy_work = internal / (internal + external); autonomy_material = (active_C + fixation_C) / supply_C; autonomy = (internal + (active_C + fixation_C) dG_C) / (internal + external + supply_C dG_C).
assumptions: Carbon is priced at a fixed free-energy equivalent when work and material are combined.

population_budget.doc:
Carry the lineage's net budget into a population of real individuals.

Each tick the lineage's co-limited gain — ``min(material_net, net_power /
carbon_energy_equivalent)`` mol C (og-08's Liebig minimum: the scarcer of
carbon and the work to fix it; a deficit on either side is a loss) —
enters the ``localized`` biomass reservoir (a gain) or is drawn from the
individuals (a deficit);
the amount is published as ``external_flux`` so the rewrite ledger closes
exactly. Individuals then take matter from the reservoir (up to
``uptake_cap`` each, while the population is below ``max_population``) and
their ``division_state`` tracks matter / ``division_mass``: the Phase-5
``DivisionStep`` divides them at 1 (``_divide``, matter halved) and the
individuals starved below ``min_matter`` are removed here by the Phase-5
``_remove`` rewrite (their matter reported as ``removed_matter`` for the
rewrite ledger). ``survivors`` = alive / initial (capped at 1), og-08's
readout from a count.

_contract.summary: The lineage budget as a population of individuals: biomass reservoir in / out (declared external_flux), growth to division, starvation to extinction.
_contract.description: gain = min(material_net, net_power / dG_C) dt; >= 0 -> reservoir, < 0 -> drawn from individuals; individuals fill from the reservoir and divide at matter = division_mass.

outputs.external_flux: moles entering (> 0) / leaving (< 0) the audited system this tick

division.doc:
``_divide`` any individual whose division_state has reached 1.0. The split
halves ``internal_amounts`` (moles) and ``volume`` — the daughters' amounts
sum to the mother's (partition residual 0) and the concentration is preserved
— and increments each daughter's generation.

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

rewrite_ledger.doc:
Conservation audit for the Phase-5 structural rewrites (``_add`` /
``_divide`` / ``_remove``) on the ``agents`` map (FMP §5.3).

Tracks the total matter (summed ``internal_amounts``) in the
(agents + localized) system. Boundary formation moves matter localized→agent
and division is agent-internal, so both leave the system total invariant;
lysis/extinction remove an individual's matter (a reported outflow). Hence
``rewrite_residual = |Δtotal + removed_matter|`` must stay ~0 across every
rewrite. ``partition_residual`` (the daughters' amounts summing to the
mother's on ``_divide``) is passed through from :class:`DivisionStep`. The
single ``rewrite_ok`` flag is the Phase-5 exit criterion's conservation gate.
The optional ``external_flux`` input (Phase 9; 0 when unwired) lets a lineage
budget feed / drain the audited system through a declared channel without
breaking the audit of the rewrites themselves.

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

lineage_stats.doc:
Read-only lineage statistics over the agents map: the population size, the
deepest generation reached (``persistence`` carries the generation counter),
and the total volume (conserved across divisions — daughter volumes sum to the
mother). Drives the og-growth-alt gates.

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

event_log.doc:
Record every structural transition of the integrated world as an event:
heredity attachment / detachment, the store charging past half / collapsing,
the work and material budgets changing sign, divisions, extinctions, the
loss of machinery and the lineage's extinction. The ablation step logs its
own phases into the same tree.

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).

_contract.summary: type(object) -> the object's type
_contract.description: type(name, bases, dict, **kwds) -> a new type

heredity_attachment.doc:
Attach heredity only when the matched budgets and the class's copy fidelity allow it.

Reads the shared precursor pools (molar) and the energy store (J) and
publishes ``attached`` = 1 when all three hold for the configured class:

* precursor budget: molecules of the class's primary pool >=
  ``attach_min_copies * cost_per_copy * n_individuals``;
* energy budget: quanta in the store >= ``attach_energy_margin *
  attach_min_copies * quanta_per_copy * n_individuals``;
* fidelity floor (Eigen 1971): the class's expected whole-state copy
  fidelity ``Q >= 1 / selective_superiority``.

``attachment_margin`` is the smallest of the three ratios (>= 1 means
attached). Once attached a lineage stays attached (``latch``), so a
transient budget dip does not sever inheritance; replication simply
stalls while a budget is exhausted. The precursor / energy thresholds are
``hypothetical`` until the expert supplies defensible ones; the study
sweeps them.

_contract.summary: Conditional heredity attachment: precursor budget, energy budget and the Eigen fidelity floor must all be met.
_contract.description: FMP section 2.5: heredity is absent until it can be paid for and copied. Each tick the step reads the shared precursor pools and the energy store, converts them to molecules / quanta per individual and compares them with the configured class's cost per copy; attached = 1 when the precursor ratio, the energy ratio and Q / (1/sigma) are all >= 1. Thresholds attach_min_copies and attach_energy_margin are hypothetical (expert decision pending) and swept; the fidelity floor is Eigen's error threshold.

outputs.fidelity_floor: 1/sigma — the Eigen threshold the class's Q must exceed

math: attach iff N_pool >= m c_p N and quanta >= k m c_q N and Q >= 1/sigma
